newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajikistan expects $185 mln in grants for 1997.
newsitem.headline: Tajikistan expects $185 mln in grants for 1997.

text.p: War-torn Tajikistan expects to receive around $185 million in grants in 1997 from donor countries and international lending institutions, the prime minister said on Tuesday.

Yakhe Azimov told a news conference in the capital Dushanbe that donor countries at a World Bank meeting in Tokyo last week said the Central Asian nation's economic needs had changed from that of "emergency aid" to "economic development".
He said most of the money would go toward technical and financial support for market reforms in the form of grants and said the sum was twice the amount of aid granted in 1995.
"The EBRD (European Bank for Reconstruction and Development) has said it is looking to increase its programme of support for small and medium size private businesses," Azimov said.
He said a team from the World Bank was scheduled to arrive in Dushanbe later this month to work on privatisation.
The former Soviet republic has been wracked by a bloody four-year civil war costing tens of thousands of lives but fighting which flared in August has since died down.
